title: Sponsor Claims Audits under the PBM Services Agreement: Annual Allowance, Notice, Lookback and Findings
content:
**Clause A — Right to audit.** The plan sponsor may start the number of claims audits per contract year that its pricing arrangement allows, with the arrangement's period of written notice in calendar days, each audit covering at most the arrangement's lookback in months of claims, ending on the notice date.

**Clause B — Acceptance.** An audit request is accepted only when the sponsor has not used its audits for the contract year.

**Clause C — Findings.** An audit finding owed to the sponsor is credited as a billing error credit memo.

## How audits used in the year are counted

- The contract year runs from the latest anniversary of the agreement's go-live date up to the present day.
- The audits used are the audit requests on this PBM Services Agreement within that contract year that are not cancelled; a cancelled audit request does not count.
- The count is read from the agreement's service request records, not from the sponsor's recollection.
- A request is accepted only while that count is below the number of audits the arrangement allows per contract year.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical, for an arrangement allowing one audit per contract year)

| Audit requests on the agreement in the current contract year | Counted as used | New audit request accepted |
|---|---|---|
| None | 0 | Yes |
| One, cancelled | 0 | Yes |
| One, not cancelled | 1 | No |
| One not cancelled, in the previous contract year only | 0 | Yes |

## Scope of an audit (hypothetical)

With a hypothetical lookback of 12 months and a written audit notice dated on the 15th of a month, the audit may reach back over at most the 12 months of claims ending on that notice date. The written notice must precede the start of the audit by at least the arrangement's notice period; under a hypothetical 60-day period, an audit noticed on day 0 starts no sooner than day 60.

## Findings

Where the completed audit reports an amount owed to the sponsor, that amount is credited to the sponsor as a credit memo for a billing error.
